title: Dilate to chest-wall depth only
view: Sagittal cross-section of one intercostal space, lateral chest wall. Head at top, skin on the left, deep to the right.
teachingPoint: The dilator goes only through the measured chest-wall depth, stopping at the parietal pleura. The wire stays beyond its tip, and the lung is not approached.
claims: Head at top, skin on the left; layers run skin, fat, intercostal muscle with ribs, parietal pleura, pleural fluid, lung.
The neurovascular bundle is three cut ends under the upper rib, vein, artery, nerve from top to bottom.
The tract crosses the space below the bundle, above the lower rib (mid-space rather than hugging the lower rib).
The dilator is one continuous piece with a length still outside the skin, so it is not driven to its hub.
The dilator tip tents the parietal pleura and goes no further; the guidewire exits the tip into the fluid with a J curve that does not touch the lung.
The cyan bracket spans skin to parietal pleura: the chest-wall depth measured on ultrasound.
The base art has no text or watermark; the two labels are drawn by code: Parietal pleura, Measured depth.

geometry.why: the depth bracket starts at the skin, left of the dilator tip
